title: Azure Portal and Cloud Shell
description: Learn how to navigate the Azure Portal and use Azure Cloud Shell from your browser.

data.text: The **Azure Portal** (portal.azure.com) is a web-based console for managing every part of Azure. **Cloud Shell** is a browser-based terminal that gives you a pre-installed Azure CLI and PowerShell environment without installing anything on your computer.

data.title: Portal Essentials
items: **Home** — Your personalized dashboard with pinned resources
**All services** — Browse every Azure service by category
**Resource groups** — View and manage all your resource groups
**Cost Management** — Track your spending and set budgets
**Search bar** — Quickly find resources, services, and documentation

data.text: When you open a resource, the left-hand menu shows options like Overview, Activity Log, Access Control, and Settings. These options change depending on the resource type.

Cloud Shell opens a terminal directly in the browser. It automatically authenticates you, so you do not need to run `az login` separately. You can choose between Bash and PowerShell environments. Your files persist between sessions because Cloud Shell attaches an Azure Files share.

data.title: Cloud Shell Commands
data.code:
# List your subscriptions
az account list --output table

# Set the default subscription
az account set --subscription "MySubscription"

# List resource groups
az group list --output table

# Show details for a specific resource group
az group show --name MyAppResourceGroup

data.text: Bash vs PowerShell in Cloud Shell

data.title: Use Cloud Shell for Quick Tasks
data.text: Cloud Shell is perfect for quick commands when you are away from your normal workstation. For longer scripts, install the Azure CLI or PowerShell locally.

terms.definition: The web-based console for managing Azure resources visually.
A browser-based terminal with Azure CLI and PowerShell, pre-authenticated and persistent storage.
A cloud file share service used by Cloud Shell to persist files between sessions.

items.text: Open the Azure Portal and locate the search bar
Create a resource group using the Portal
Open Cloud Shell and switch between Bash and PowerShell
Run `az group list` in Cloud Shell to see your resource groups
